I'm checking a few edge cases for the extension helper: it takes the first segment after the first dot and lowercases nothing, so 'Archive.TAR.GZ' gives 'TAR' and 'photo.JPG' gives 'JPG', which would fall through to octet-stream. Next I'm looking at the filename sanitizer, where slashes become underscores, so traversal strings like 'a/../../etc' should be harmless, and a '..' sitting mid-name such as 'foo..bar' seems fine too.

I'm noticing that stripping the leading dots and then replacing slashes can leave a name that's empty, since '..' on its own collapses to nothing. I'm also seeing that '.htaccess' loses its dot and so its extension. I'll run a few quick tests to confirm these cases.

payload.text:
**I don't think this should merge yet.** `extensionOf` doesn't do what the README says, so `contentType` returns the wrong type for many normal filenames. I didn't change anything; I only read the diff and ran the functions on some edge cases.

**Blocker: `src/extension.js`**
`name.split('.')[1]` takes the text after the *first* dot and doesn't lowercase it. The README says the extension is the text after the *last* dot, lowercased. Here's what it returns now:

| input | returns | README expects | content type you get |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Archive.TAR.GZ` | `"TAR"` | `gz` | octet-stream (should be gzip) |
| `photo.JPG` | `"JPG"` | `jpg` | octet-stream (should be image/jpeg) |
| `my.photo.png` | `"photo"` | `png` | octet-stream (should be image/png) |
| `README` | `undefined` | `""` | octet-stream |
| `file.` | `""` | `""` | octet-stream ✓ |

Uppercase extensions and names with more than one dot both get the wrong type. The no-dot case returns `undefined` instead of the empty string the README promises. A fix along these lines would work: find the last dot, return `""` if there isn't one, otherwise return the lowercased text after it.

**Gap in `src/safe-name.js`**
- Stored names can't climb a directory. `../`, `a/../../b` → `a_.._.._b` and encoded dots are all handled.
- But `..`, `...` and `../` come out as an empty string. An empty stored name could overwrite something or point at the upload directory itself. It should fall back to a placeholder or be rejected.
- `.htaccess` becomes `htaccess`. That's probably fine, but it's a quiet rename worth knowing about.

**Tests**
They pass only because each covers a single easy case (`photo.jpg`, `../my file.png`). The table above, plus the empty-name cases, would make good test cases. There are no tests for `contentType` at all.

**Minor**
- The changelog mentions content types but not `safeName`.
- `TYPES` has no `jpeg`, so `photo.jpeg` will come back as octet-stream.
